clue.text: Impressed a sailor without his knowing!

definitions.text: Impressed a sailor without his knowing!

parts.words: Impressed a sailor without his knowing!
parts.note: impressed here means forced into naval service, as press gangs once did to unwary men in port

explanation.surface: Someone made an impression on a sailor who never noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' reads as 'made an impression on', but the sense is press-ganged: seized for a ship's crew, often after being drugged or tricked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kidnapped onto a ship's crew by trickery is the classic meaning of the word, named after the Chinese port.

clue.text: Huge portion of chicken or moussaka

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner asks for a generous helping of either chicken or moussaka.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both words mean very large in size.

clue.text: American girls seen in Norfolk

definitions.meaning: in US slang a broad is a woman
the Norfolk ... are a network of shallow lakes and rivers in eastern England

explanation.surface: Young women from the States spotted on holiday in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is a county in eastern England; its Broads are a famous boating district.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for women, and also the name of the waterways that Norfolk is known for.

clue.text: Hothead raised the stake

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: Etna is a volcano, a mountain with a hot head

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered gambler pushes the stakes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hothead' looks like an angry person; it is the Sicilian volcano, read upwards by 'raised'.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the stake each player puts in before dealing is called this.

clue.text: They go to court to protect workers

parts.note: to defend is to protect
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: People taking a case to court to shield employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Accused people must appear in court to answer charges, so they are the ones who go there.

clue.text: Ranch where Incas ate, when working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A farm where the ancient Incas took their meals during work.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American cattle farm or estate goes by this Spanish name.

clue.text: Clear half the street

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: An order to empty half the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear condensation from a windscreen or mirror is the meaning here.

clue.text: Astound without ado

indicators.note: without tells us to take away the letters of the following word from the word before it

explanation.surface: To amaze someone at once, with no fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A, D and O out of 'Astound' leaves the answer, and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze or amaze someone suddenly is a synonym of astound.

clue.text: Straying in herd can result in obstruction

indicators.note: straying means wandering off, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Cattle wandering from the herd can cause a blockage.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstruction is something that gets in the way, an impediment.

clue.text: Paper put to bed

definitions.meaning: linen laid on a bed when it is made up

explanation.surface: A newspaper being sent to press, in the trade's phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put to bed' is newspaper slang for sending an edition to print, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of paper and a piece of bed linen both carry this name.

clue.text: Managed to be back before class to make report

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
be back says the word is written in reverse

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A manager returns ahead of a lesson to give an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or give an account of events is to report them.

clue.text: Euphoria makes family member lose her head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a relation is a family member

explanation.surface: A relative so happy she loses control.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean intense joy or high spirits.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval by motorists or Scotsmen

definitions.text: Expression of disapproval by motorists or Scotsmen

parts.words: Expression of disapproval by motorists or Scotsmen
parts.note: drivers sound their horns in annoyance, and a Scot cries 'och' or 'toots' type exclamations of irritation

explanation.surface: Drivers and Scots both show their disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: Motorists blare their horns; Scots say 'hoots!', a traditional Scottish exclamation of impatience.
explanation.definitionFit: Car horn blasts and a jeering crowd's noise both go by this name, as does a Scottish exclamation.

clue.text: Gives up office from basic date

indicators.note: from says the answer is made out of the letters that follow, reworked

explanation.surface: Someone resigns from a job starting on a basic date.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchs and officials renounce a throne or post this way.

clue.text: Run and puff — clergyman required

parts.note: a puff is a piece of promotion, an advert
a minister is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman out of breath needs to jog and pant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run and puff' suggests exercise; 'Run' is the definition and 'puff' a plug.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or estate is to manage it.

clue.text: Fulfilling the conditions by paying in full

definitions.meaning: meeting the requirements, as in meeting a test
settling a debt completely, as in meeting a creditor's claim

explanation.surface: Meeting a contract's terms by settling the whole bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means meeting requirements, and also discharging a debt in full.

clue.text: One just plays at work

parts.note: a person whose job is to play music, rather than someone idle

explanation.surface: A slacker who does nothing but mess about at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' suggests idling; the sense is playing music for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who performs on an instrument is literally paid to play.

clue.text: OK for car to be adapted — it's for carrying more luggage

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It's fine for a car to be modified to hold extra bags.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame fixed on top of a car lets it carry extra baggage.

clue.text: Understood I am parking legally

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A driver insists their parking is legal and understood as such.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied but not stated is tacitly understood.

clue.text: Doesn't take into consideration special reductions

definitions.meaning: to discount something is to disregard it

explanation.surface: A shop overlooks its own sale offers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means disregards, and also price cuts offered to buyers.

clue.text: Dancer to see in uniform

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: uniform means unvarying, the same
lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: Someone goes to watch a dancer in military dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Salome danced for Herod in the Bible and asked for John the Baptist's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical figure famed for the dance of the seven veils.

clue.text: Manages to provide clothing for priests

definitions.meaning: long cloaks worn by priests in processions

explanation.surface: Someone manages to supply priests with vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means gets by, and also the long ceremonial cloaks clergy wear.

clue.text: Is able to get five to like the artist's work

parts.note: can means is able
V is the Roman numeral for five
as means like

explanation.surface: Someone manages to make five people enjoy a painter's output.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters work on stretched fabric, so a painting itself is called this.

clue.text: Bright star in spiral ring complex

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: An astronomer's description of a brilliant star in a complicated circling pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pole Star, the brightest in the Little Bear, is a bright star.

clue.text: Hounds prepare to travel

definitions.meaning: to fill a suitcase before a trip

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs get ready for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of hunting dogs, and also the act of filling a suitcase.

clue.text: A night in Paris breaks into any kind of regular income!

indicators.note: breaks into says one piece is set inside another

parts.note: nuit is French for night

explanation.surface: A burglar's night in Paris yields a steady income.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed sum paid yearly, often bought with a pension pot, is a regular income.

clue.text: Third man sounds competent

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: A third person on the team seems capable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, after Adam and his first son Cain, Abel is the third man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's second son, the third male human in the Bible.

clue.text: Cause of cracks that can bring down the house

definitions.text: Cause of cracks that can bring down the house

parts.words: Cause of cracks that can bring down the house
parts.note: cracks are jokes, and bringing down the house means drawing huge laughter

explanation.surface: A structural fault that could make a building collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surveyor's language hides a stand-up performer telling wisecracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up entertainer makes the jokes that win roaring laughter.

clue.text: Part of plans for promotion?

definitions.meaning: an architect's drawing of a building's face
raising someone to a higher rank

explanation.surface: An employee asks whether there is a step up in the plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Architects' drawings include side views of this name, and a rise in rank is another.
